Hi all —

I reviewed the draft exhibit and pulled a concise set of redline suggestions to keep language aligned with Redwood's standard risk posture while addressing MediSphere's audit needs. High-level notes below; see attached MSA_redlines_v1.pdf for markup.

Key legal points:
- Audit scope: we propose language that allows collection of evidence (logs, configuration snapshots) and on-site inspection only for things scoped to the dedicated account or tenant. Multi-tenant production systems remain subject to constraints; we provide sample logs and diagrams instead.
- Pen test carveouts: Redwood will permit third-party tests against a customer-dedicated staging environment; any test against shared production components must be mutually agreed and limited to non-disruptive techniques.
- Notice & remediation: 2-week notice for standard windows; emergency expedited windows may be accommodated with an approval clause and defined SLA for mitigation obligations.
- Confidentiality: all results and reports will be treated as confidential; we add an NDA reference and a clause limiting distribution beyond named reviewers.

Next steps for contract coordination:
- I'll upload the marked MSA and a clean exhibit to the DocuSign packet if procurement requests a redline set. Grace: if MediSphere's procurement is ready, indicate a preferred DocuSign routing and I'll queue the legal countersign.

Mark — happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you'd like to walk through specific redline language before procurement circulates.
